quote: Compared to controls, 10 proteins were increased in serum of both diseases, including Th1 (IFN-γ, CXCL9, TNF-β) and Th17 (CCL20) markers.
summary: Serum CXCL9 was increased in atopic dermatitis and psoriasis versus controls and correlated with skin levels; not a UC study.

quote: Treatment of ECs with PPARgamma activators significantly inhibited IFN-gamma-induced mRNA and protein expression of the CXC chemokines IFN-inducible protein of 10 kDa (IP-10), monokine induced by IFN-gamma (Mig), and IFN-inducible T-cell alpha-chemoattractant (I-TAC), whereas expression of the CC chemokine monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 was not altered.
summary: PPARgamma activators reduced IFN-gamma-induced Mig (CXCL9) mRNA and protein in endothelial cells, suggesting less T cell recruitment.

quote: These cells exhibited a distinct arrangement of pro-inflammatory and interferon response genes, including elevated levels of CXCL10, CXCL9, CCL2, CCL3, GBP1, STAT1, and IL1B.
summary: CXCL9 is elevated in an IFN-gamma and TNF-driven inflammatory macrophage state found in inflamed UC colon, Crohn's ileum, RA synovium and COVID-19 lung.

quote: Treatment enhanced IFNγ and CXCL9/CXCL10 expression, systemic IFNγ/TNFα production, and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, indicating an immunostimulatory environment.
summary: Olaparib plus durvalumab raised CXCL9/CXCL10 expression in ovarian cancer biopsies; not a UC study.

quote: Patients who developed irAEs had lower levels of CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11 and CXCL19 at baseline and exhibited greater increases in CXCL9 and CXCL10 levels at post treatment compared to patients without irAEs.
summary: Serum CXCL9 levels at baseline and change on treatment were associated with immune-related adverse events in checkpoint inhibitor patients.

quote: The macrophage compartment was heterogeneous and displayed marked enrichment in an inflammatory CCR2+ subpopulation highly expressing Cxcl9 (chemokine [C-X-C motif] ligand 9), Cxcl10 (chemokine [C-X-C motif] ligand 10), Gbp2b (interferon-induced guanylate-binding protein 2b), and Fcgr4 (Fc receptor, IgG low affinity IV) that originated from CCR2+ monocytes.
summary: Cxcl9 marks an expanded inflammatory macrophage subpopulation in mouse checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis; not a colitis study.

quote: For the first time, we showed (and validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry) that intestinal macrophages in patients with IBD present both M1 and M2 features, as recently described for tumor-associated macrophages, that affect key pathways for IBD pathology, represented by key markers such as MMP12 (fibrosis), CXCL9 (T-cell attraction), and CD40 (T-cell activation).
summary: CXCL9 is a key dysregulated marker in intestinal macrophages from UC and Crohn patients, validated by qPCR and immunohistochemistry.
The alias cmk appears only in the inhibitor Ac-YVAD-cmk; the paper concerns NETs and AIM2 in ARDS, not CXCL9.

quote: Our study also revealed that the intestinal stem cell marker OLFM4 is expressed at very low levels in fetal intestine and in HIOs, but is robust in adult crypts.
summary: OLFM4 is low in fetal intestine and human intestinal organoids but robust in adult crypts; a development study, not UC.

quote: Sporadic failure of Cre-mediated Hsp60 deletion gives rise to hyperproliferative crypt foci originating from OLFM4+ stem cells.
summary: OLFM4 is used only as a stem cell marker in an HSP60 mitochondrial dysfunction study.

quote: STAT3 was activated (phosphorylated) in inflamed colon tissues from Mefv-/-, which also had increased expression of stem cell markers (OLFM4, BMI1, and MSI1) compared with colons from control mice.
summary: Olfm4 is one of three stem cell markers raised in colitic Mefv knockout mice; the paper's focus is pyrin.

quote: Production and expression of proinflammatory cytokines/chemokines such as IL-1beta, IL-5, IL-12 p70, and MIP-1alpha was increased in OLFM4 KO mice compared with infected controls.
summary: OLFM4 knockout mice had lower H. pylori load but more gastric inflammation and cytokines, so OLFM4 restrains NF-kappaB-driven inflammation.

quote: This is characterized by intestinal stem cell (ISC) expansion as shown by an inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (Ire1α)-mediated increase in Lgr5(+) and Olfm4(+) ISCs and a Stat3-dependent increase in the proliferative output of transit-amplifying cells.
summary: Olfm4 marks expanded intestinal stem cells in Xbp1 hypomorphic mice; it is a marker, not the subject.

quote: Treatment of organoids exposed to DSS with Reg3B or propionate reversed the chemical injury with a loss of expression of the stem-cell marker Lgr5 and Olfm4.
summary: Olfm4 is a stem cell marker read out in organoids in a Reg3B and propionate colitis study.

quote: IECs expressing IKK2ca displayed altered Wnt signaling and increased proliferation and elevated expression of genes encoding intestinal stem cell-associated factors including Ascl2, Olfm4, DLK1, and Bmi-1, indicating that increased IKK2/NF-κB activation synergized with Wnt signaling to drive intestinal tumorigenesis.
summary: Olfm4 is one of several stem cell genes elevated in IKK2-activated intestinal epithelium in a tumor model.

quote: A population of intestinal LGR5/OLFM4-positive stem/progenitor cells were interspersed between goblet-like cells within the crypt-base.
summary: OLFM4 marks stem/progenitor cells at the base of native human colonic crypts in a Wnt and BMP renewal study.

quote: Several members of the family have been implicated in various common diseases, notably myocilin in glaucoma and OLFM4 in cancer.
summary: Review of the olfactomedin protein family that mentions OLFM4 in cancer without colitis data.

quote: Zip7 deficiency led to the loss of Olfm4+ intestinal stem cells and the degeneration of post-mitotic Paneth cells, indicating a fundamental requirement for Zip7 in homeostatic intestinal regeneration.
summary: Olfm4 is used as an intestinal stem cell marker lost in Zip7-deficient mice.

quote: Selective expression of Reg 1alpha and GW112 genes in the crypt epithelium of inflamed colonic mucosa suggests the important regulatory functions of these genes.
summary: GW112 (OLFM4) is upregulated in crypt epithelium of inflamed colonic mucosa in IBD.

quote: These results indicate that OLFM4 is an important negative regulator of neutrophil bactericidal activity by restricting cathepsin C activity and its downstream granule-associated serine proteases.
summary: OLFM4 knockout mice cleared bacteria better and resisted sepsis more, showing OLFM4 restrains neutrophil killing; an infection model, not colitis.

quote: Functional analysis of the predictor genes showed that they play a role in immune responses to bacteria (PTN, OLFM4 and LILRA2), autophagy and endocytocis processes (ATG16L1, DNAJC6, VPS26B, RABGEF1, ITSN1 and TMEM127) and glucocorticoid receptor degradation (STS and MMD2).
summary: OLFM4 is one of several predictor genes in an IBD biopsy expression classifier, without a specific result.

quote: ISC-marker genes, OLFM4 and SLC12A2, were expressed by an increased number of small intestinal epithelial cells in the active lesion of CD.
summary: More small intestinal epithelial cells expressed OLFM4 in active Crohn's lesions; organoids showed comparable OLFM4 levels.

quote: Genes encoding intestinal stem cell markers BMI1 and OLFM4 are upregulated in the colon of Nlrc3-/- mice.
summary: OLFM4 is upregulated as a stem cell marker in Nlrc3-deficient mouse colon; the paper focuses on NLRC3.

quote: In addition, Olfm4 deletion significantly enhanced intestinal-crypt proliferation and inflammation induced by azoxymethane/dextran sodium sulfate.
summary: Olfm4 deletion promoted colon tumors in Apc-Min mice and worsened AOM/DSS-induced inflammation, showing OLFM4 restrains Wnt and NF-kappaB signaling.

quote: In contrast, OLFM4 is expressed in the gastric phenotype of GC.
summary: OLFM4 is upregulated in gastric cancer and associated with the gastric mucin phenotype; not a UC study.
